correctness.rationale: The graph is the Cayley graph of F_2^4 with XOR generators 1,2,4,8,15. An independent implementation rebuilt all 120 independent four-sets, verified the Alexander dual on all 65,536 vertex masks, and enumerated 52,915 and 12,621 augmented faces. Lexicographic element matchings give 26,434 and 6,287 pairs; independent directed-cover topological sorts traverse all 392,720 and 70,368 incidences with no cycles. Exact signed integral cancellation gives K critical counts {6:1,7:1,8:45}, d7=(2), d8=0 and B counts {5:45,6:1,7:1}, d6=0,d7=(-2). These finite exhaustive calculations verify the complete chain reductions and Smith factors Z/2 and free rank 45; the standard acyclic Morse theorem gives CW models with no low positive-dimensional cells, establishing five-/four-connectivity and K non-shellability because pure dimension is 11 but H6 != 0. No higher attaching maps or wedge decomposition were inferred.
residual_risks: Full homotopy types and higher attaching maps are not established and are not asserted.
Computational proof is exhaustive only for this specified sixteen-vertex graph, not an infinite family.
Raw mod-two ranks alone could not certify integral torsion; signed integral boundary was separately computed.

value.rationale: The 16-vertex Clebsch graph is a standard connected, 5-regular, triangle-free strongly regular graph, providing a motivated high-symmetry test for the natural total-four-cut filtration. Exact two-torsion and free degree-eight homology in a pure 11-dimensional complex, together with the dual integral calculation, identify a concrete failure of all-sphere-wedge and shellability behavior not furnished by previously classified graph families. Though finite, the pair of full Smith decompositions and connectivity are structural facts one can reuse when testing stronger classification conjectures; their value does not rest on a claimed general family or on merely rerunning known tables.
residual_risks: Scientific value is for a canonical finite exact instance rather than a general characterization.
No full homotopy splitting, family extension or novel generic torsion theorem follows from this proof.
